newsitem.title: SPAIN: Basque separatist found hanged in Spanish prison.
newsitem.headline: Basque separatist found hanged in Spanish prison.

text.p: An ETA Basque separatist rebel was found hanged in his Spanish jail cell late on Sunday, prison officials said in a statement.

Prison warders in a jail in central Spain found Juan Carlos Hernando, 35, who was serving a six-year sentence for collaboration with an armed band, hanged with his hands loosely bound in front of him.

Hernando was alone in his cell, suspended from a water pipe by a plastic cord "similar to the kind used to adjust sports clothing". Another cord that appeared to be a shoelace was wrapped around his hands with no knots tied.
The Albacete prison doctor tried to revive him without success, the statement said.
Prison officials said they were opening an investigation into Hernando's death as was usual in "an event of these circumstances".
ETA, which has killed some 800 people in a nearly 30-year campaign for Basque independence, murdered a young politician last week sparking national outrage.

The guerrilla group kidnapped Miguel Angel Blanco on July 10 and threatened to kill him 48 hours later if the government did not meet its demand that the 500-odd ETA inmates scattered across the country be transferred to jails in the northern Basque region.
The government refused, calling it blackmail, and ETA shot Blanco in the head on July 12. He died the following day.
Millions of Spaniards took to the streets in protest. Eight ETA prisoners have since condemned the attack. Most of them had previously renounced adherence to ETA's armed struggle.
